Memphis logotype drawing

Christoph Radl’s artwork for the Memphis wordmark: squared white capitals over a patterned underline.

Source
Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam: Memphis (2010.1.0588)
Creator
Christoph Radl (designer); Sottsass Associati and Memphis (clients)
Made
1982
Style
Memphis (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Bold, graphic, geometric
Evidence
Downloaded the museum’s published image (640 × 466 px) from the Stedelijk Museum to a private scratchpad and inspected it with the Read tool on 2026-09-25. No image is stored in the catalogue. The museum’s file carries a “NO REPRO QUALITY” stamp.
Reviewed
25 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The Stedelijk classes this as a drawing by Christoph Radl, 1982, 34.7 × 47.5 cm, with Sottsass Associati and Memphis as clients. Stedelijk record.

Interni says Radl began working with Ettore Sottsass in 1980, “designing the image of Memphis”, and later curated the 2022 Triennale exhibition “Memphis Again”. Interni: Memphis Again.

Observed

  • White capitals “MEMPHIS” sit on a black rectangle mounted on a white board.
  • The letters are built from rectangles; the M has a notched, stepped middle, and some strokes end in angled cuts.
  • Under each letter group runs a short bar of fine black-and-white pattern, broken into segments.
  • Tape and registration marks around the board show that it is working artwork.

Why it belongs

The wordmark is heavy and simple, which lets it sit on top of the group’s busy patterns. The patterned underline brings the laminate language into the type.

Borrow

Pair a heavy, squared display wordmark with a thin patterned rule under it.

Put the wordmark in white on a solid black band when it must work over pattern.

The same letterforms appear on the Memphis swatch card and the 1983 leaflet.
